The original parameters were chosen as follows: ds was 0.1 mm, dz 0.1 mm, f p 0.8, and v 250 mm/s, with S-cross scanning in x and y directions. Higher energy density is needed for fabricating NbMoTaW HEA parts, so there was an additional remelting process, which had the same parameters as the original process but underwent remelting twice for each layer, which means that there was 3 times the laser energy input.

research_thread.scientific_problem: How to achieve homogeneous solid solution formation in NbMoTaW refractory High Entropy Alloys (HEAs) via SLM given high melting points and differential element absorption/melting behaviors.
research_thread.sample_lineage: Mixed powders (Nb, Mo, Ta, W) -> Mechanical milling -> Drying -> SLM (1x pass) -> SLM (3x pass with 2 remelts).
research_thread.intervention: Increased linear energy density to ~2.83 J/mm by adding 2 remelting passes (3x total energy) on top of baseline parameters (500 W, 250 mm/s).
research_thread.baseline: Single SLM pass with linear energy density of 0.943 J/mm.
research_thread.conditions: Argon atmosphere (O2 < 20 ppm), Cuboid samples (10x10x0.5 mm), Cu target XRD, SEM, EDS.
research_thread.structure: Single BCC solid solution with extremely fine grains (13.4 μm) and dendrites (6.59 μm); negative composition deviations for Mo (-0.16 at%) and Nb (-3.5 at%).
research_thread.outcome: Formation of single BCC phase; excellent microhardness and corrosion resistance (2 orders of magnitude better than 316L steel); observed segregation due to powder properties.
research_thread.mechanism: High energy input required to overcome high melting points and differential absorption rates (A_Mo > A_W > A_Nb > A_Ta) to ensure complete melting and reduce segregation.
research_thread.hypothesis_value: High energy density via remelting is a necessary and effective strategy to homogenize refractory HEAs with high melting point disparities, provided absorption rate uncertainties are managed.
alternative_explanations: Segregation might be inherent to the rapid cooling rates of SLM regardless of energy density.
Powder morphology (spherical/near-spherical) and size distribution might dominate deviation over energy input alone.
boundaries: Absorption rate assumptions in energy density calculations may introduce error.
High melting point limits traditional casting (1800°C insufficient).
null_or_negative_results: Negative deviations in molar ratio for Mo and Nb (no more than 5%) persist despite high energy.
Specific limitations of the absorption rate assumption.
missing_information: Direct quantitative comparison of microstructural features (grain size, segregation extent) between 1x and 3x energy samples.
Quantitative measurement of residual stress or porosity levels resulting from the 3x energy input.
